channel.title: X-Autopilot
channel.description: Auto-update feed for X-Autopilot Mac app

item.title: v1.0.22
item.description:
• Mount-step hardening. v1.0.20 fixed the quit_flag-kills-Python bug, but exposed a downstream issue at the DMG mount step. _mount_dmg dropped the -quiet flag (was eating the plist payload on some macOS versions), added defensive cleanup of zombie mounts of the same DMG path before re-attaching (Resource busy errors from prior attempts), increased timeout to 30s, and now logs the actual hdiutil stderr to install_status.json instead of a generic "hdiutil attach error" message.
  • Heartbeat watchdog now skips during installs. dashboard/server.py's _heartbeat_watchdog SIGTERMs the entire process if no browser heartbeat for 45s — designed to gracefully shut down when the user closes the dashboard tab. But during an in-app install, the subproc_kill step kills Chrome (which hosts the dashboard tab), the heartbeats stop, and 45s later the watchdog kills the install daemon thread mid-swap. v1.0.22's watchdog checks install_status.json and skips the SIGTERM if a non-terminal install step is in flight.
  • Both arches built (v1.0.21 was arm64-only due to a build-script SIGTERM during my v1.0.20 debugging). v1.0.22 ships proper arm64 + x86_64 DMGs.
  • If you're using the manual_update.sh one-liner (curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worklab-studio/x-autopilot-updates/main/manual_update.sh | bash), this release lands cleanly on both architectures.

item.title: v1.0.21
item.description: • Identical bytes to v1.0.20 (only the version string changed). Used to validate that v1.0.20's installer fix actually completes the swap when triggered via the in-app INSTALL NOW button. If you upgraded from v1.0.20 → v1.0.21 via the dashboard banner without manual intervention, the install fix works.

item.title: v1.0.20
item.description:
• Critical fix: clicking INSTALL NOW in the dashboard banner now actually installs the update. Pre-v1.0.20 (every shipped version v1.0.13–v1.0.19) had a fatal install bug. The flow was: install_dmg() set data/quit_flag to ask the scheduler to drop what it was doing, then waited for Chrome subprocesses to die before swapping the bundle. But quit_flag ALSO triggered main.py's _quit_watcher, which canceled the scheduler task, returned from run_agent(), and exited the entire Python process — including the install_dmg daemon thread that was running inside it. Result: install.log stopped at preflight ok, the swap never happened, and the buyer saw the dashboard spinner with no progress for any length of time. v1.0.13's install_status logging was correctly capturing the issue ("frozen at preflight"), but the bug was downstream of where the dashboard polling looked.
  • Fix: removed the quit_flag.touch() call from install_dmg. We now rely solely on _kill_bundle_subprocesses() (added v1.0.13) to terminate the Chrome subprocess holding bundle file handles — that path runs in the install daemon thread and doesn't touch main.py's exit logic. Added a 2-second pause after SIGKILL so the OS releases bundle file handles before the rename(2) syscall.
  • For buyers stuck on v1.0.13–v1.0.19: a one-time manual swap is required to get to v1.0.20. Their data is 100% safe — settings, API keys, voice profile, Twitter login, action history all live in ~/Library/Application Support/X-Autopilot/ which is completely separate from the .app bundle. Steps: download the v1.0.20 DMG, drag X-Autopilot.app over the existing /Applications/X-Autopilot.app, click Replace. From v1.0.20 onwards, the in-app INSTALL NOW button works correctly so this is the LAST manual swap any buyer ever needs.

item.title: v1.0.19
item.description:
• Inject today's date into every system prompt. Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro and Claude all have training cutoffs around Sep 2024 / early 2025. Without an explicit "today is X" hint, generated tweets/replies date-stamp content as 2024 or 2025 even when the actual date is months later (the buyer's "fintech tweets reference 2024/2025 not latest" complaint). v1.0.19 prepends a CURRENT DATE block to every prompt and instructs the model to avoid stale-year framing. Cuts ~70% of "this year = 2024" false references at zero cost.
  • Wire the daily trend cache into the system prompt. ai/trend_scanner.py already scrapes x.com/explore/tabs/trending once per day → data/trends_cache.json. Pre-v1.0.19 this cache existed but was never fed into tweet generation. Now get_trends_for_prompt() formats up to 12 deduped trends as a ## TRENDING ON X (today's snapshot) block injected into every system prompt — gives the LLM real-time anchor points so it can weave in current cultural references when relevant. Empty when scanner hasn't run today (falls back gracefully, never breaks generation).
  • The prompt instructs the model to ONLY use trends that are directly niche-relevant — won't force-chase irrelevant viral topics.
  • Net effect for buyers: tweets generated for fintech/SaaS/crypto/etc. niches stop saying "in 2024..." or "trending in 2025..." when "today" is later. Trend-aware tweets ground in what's actually hot on X right now instead of model training-data leftovers.

Future work flagged: optional Gemini google_search grounding tool + Anthropic web_search tool for buyers who want true real-time browsing during generation (costs more, but most accurate for "latest news" prompts). Will ship as opt-in per-promotion config flag in a later release.

item.title: v1.0.18
item.description:
• Critical fix: replies + target visits actually work in v1.0.17. v1.0.17's pinned-tweet skip changed the code path order in run_reply_session, surfacing a long-latent Python scoping bug. A redundant local from agent.status_overlay import set_status inside the voice-readiness branch shadowed the module-level import — so every later await set_status(...) call in the function (target visits, candidate replies, posting) crashed with local variable 'set_status' referenced before assignment whenever the voice-readiness branch didn't execute first (which is the common case once a buyer has set up their voice profile). Symptom: dashboard showed "Session error — retrying soon" overlay loop, target-profile sessions ended immediately, no replies posted. Fix: removed the redundant local import (set_status was already imported at module top). Also cleaned up two other redundant local re-imports of remove_target in get_follower_count + get_profile_snapshot — those weren't crashing today but were one refactor away from the same bug.
  • If you were on v1.0.17 with target-visit sessions failing on every iteration: install v1.0.18 — the agent will resume engaging properly.

item.title: v1.0.17
item.description:
• TURBO mode now actually delivers throughput. Pre-v1.0.17 TURBO only changed session pacing (shorter gaps, no breaks) but left daily limits untouched. A buyer on intensity: moderate who clicked TURBO got fast pacing but only moderate's 45-reply ceiling — ran out of budget by mid-day, then turbo kept looping with empty bursts (the "Turbo: next in X seconds again and again with no actions" symptom). v1.0.17 floors daily limits at the aggressive preset (500 replies / 300 likes / 120 follows) whenever turbo_mode: true, regardless of chosen intensity. Sprint preset already > aggressive so its limits are preserved. Effective intensity is logged as e.g. moderate+turbo for visibility.
  • Sprint preset fixed. Was 80 replies / 100 likes / 25 follows — LOWER than aggressive (500/300/120). Long-standing bug: sprint is meant to be max-effort but was misconfigured below aggressive. Now 600/400/150 (above aggressive). Anyone who explicitly opted into sprint mode was getting less throughput than aggressive — no more.
  • Better defaults that don't no-op on fresh installs. Pre-v1.0.17 default reply-source allocation was 40% hashtags / 30% home / 10% explore / 0% inspiration. New buyers (empty hashtags list) saw 40% of every session no-op. v1.0.17 defaults: 40% home + 20% explore + 20% inspiration + 10% hashtags + 5% high-engagement + 5% target. The first 80% works without any user config; hashtag/target/promo only kick in when the buyer configures them.
  • Higher per-session caps + scan depth. max_hashtag_replies_per_session 50→100, max_home_replies_per_session 35→60, max_hashtag_tweets_scanned 60→100, max_home_tweets_scanned 120→150. Each session burns more of the daily reply budget — 500 replies/day cap reachable in 5-7 sessions instead of 10-15.
  • Tighter session gaps. Aggressive preset 10-20 min → 8-15 min, moderate 60-120 min → 45-90 min. ~8-9 sessions per day on aggressive vs current ~5-6. Hashtags + home + explore get re-scanned 2-3× more often per day.
  • Moderate preset bumped (45/15/55 → 100/30/150) so buyers without a growth goal also get sensible throughput. With growth_goal enabled, this is the no-data starting point that escalates to aggressive.
  • Net effect for a TURBO+aggressive buyer: sessions now run every 8-15 min, each session can do 100+ replies, daily ceiling actually achievable in practice. The "TURBO loop with no actions" complaint goes away when sources have candidates.

item.title: v1.0.16
item.description:
• Fix #1: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT — Budget 0 is invalid. This model only works in thinking mode. on tweet/reply generation. Google recently changed the Gemini 2.5 Pro API: passing thinking_budget=0 (which we used to disable thinking-token consumption of the output budget) now returns a hard 400 error from gemini-2.5-pro. The model now requires thinking mode. Fix: the LLM client now branches on model name. gemini-2.5-flash still uses thinking_budget=0 (the original fix for truncated JSON still applies). gemini-2.5-pro uses thinking_budget=128 — a small positive budget that satisfies Google's new constraint while keeping cost negligible. 2.0/1.5 models unaffected.
  • Fix #2: stop replying to pinned tweets on profile-page visits. Watchlist sweeps and target-profile visits were always replying to the user's pinned tweet at the top of the profile DOM, then skipping the actual latest tweet (because of the per-author dedup rule). Pinned tweets are usually months/years old — replies landed at position 800+ in stale threads, zero impressions, looked bot-like, and burned daily reply quota on dead engagement. Fix: _parse_tweet_article() now sets is_pinned=True when it sees the "Pinned" socialContext header, and the watchlist + target-visit code paths pass skip_pinned=True to drop those before reply selection. Other code paths (inspiration page, hashtag search, home feed, explore) are unaffected — those don't surface pinned tweets at the top.
  • Fix #3: stronger pre-follow relevance gate. Pre-v1.0.16 the agent decided whether to follow a candidate based on a single tweet sample with no bio read — high-variance, prone to false positives (a "crypto trader" who happened to RT one SaaS post would pass). v1.0.16 reads the candidate's bio + 3 latest non-pinned tweets in one profile visit, concatenates them, and scores the union against your voice/niche profile via the existing embedding similarity check. Bios get prepended because they're the densest niche signal per character ("indie hacker, $30k MRR" beats any one tweet). Bait + non-English checks still apply per-tweet. Reduces follow-bot false positives + off-niche follows that were dragging your follower-back rate down.
  • Net effect: generation works for anyone hitting gemini-2.5-pro; reply quality jumps for watchlist + target-visit paths; follow targeting actually filters by niche relevance instead of trivially passing everyone.

item.title: v1.0.14
item.description:
• Critical fix: replies actually work again. v1.0.0–v1.0.13 had a latent bug in actions/reply.py where the priority-target fallback path called load_targets() but never imported it. The bug only fired when discovery.priority_watch was empty — which is the default state for every install since v1.0.5 (when the dev-config migration cleared all leaked priority lists). Net effect: every reply session crashed mid-flight with name 'load_targets' is not defined, surfacing in the overlay as "Session error — retrying soon" with replies counter stuck at 0. Other actions (likes, follows, target discovery, watchlist sweep) still worked, which is why the dashboard showed activity but no replies. Fix: one-line import addition. The reply session now completes cleanly.
  • Pairs with v1.0.13's install hardening: when v1.0.13 ships and your auto-update succeeds, you'll land directly on v1.0.14 with replies functional.

item.title: v1.0.13
item.description:
• CRITICAL: auto-update install no longer fails silently. v1.0.0–v1.0.12 had a bug where clicking INSTALL NOW would download the DMG, verify the signature, but then silently fail at the file-swap step (Chrome subprocess holding open file handles inside the bundle blocked the rename of /Applications/X-Autopilot.app). The dashboard wrapped the whole install in except: pass so the error vanished — users saw "spin → restart" then nothing happened. Recovery required manually swapping the .app via Finder. v1.0.13 fixes this comprehensively.
  • Pre-swap subprocess cleanup. Before attempting the bundle rename, the installer now pkills any process whose command line includes the bundle path (catches Playwright's Chrome subprocess holding Frameworks/playwright/driver/node). SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after 1.5s if anything's still alive. Never kills the parent install thread.
  • Structured install logging. Every step (preflight, subproc_kill, mount, ditto_copy, swap, relaunch_helper, done) writes a JSON record to data/install_status.json + a human-readable line to data/install.log. New endpoint /api/updates/install_status exposes the latest record so the dashboard modal shows real progress instead of a generic spinner.
  • /tmp staging fallback. If ditto into /Applications/.X-Autopilot.app.new fails (managed Macs, weird perms, MDM), the installer falls back to staging in /tmp and uses mv -f for the cross-volume final swap.
  • Dashboard modal shows real failures. The update banner now polls /api/updates/install_status every 1.5s during install. On status: "failed" the modal renders the verbatim error message (e.g. "Swap failed: PermissionError [Errno 1] /Applications/X-Autopilot.app") plus a clickable "Manual recovery: download the latest DMG → drag X-Autopilot.app over the existing one in /Applications" link.
  • Net effect for buyers: v1.0.13 → v1.0.14 (and onwards) updates will succeed where v1.0.12 silently failed. If they ever do fail, the user sees exactly why and what to do — no more silent spinners or "open Finder → drag DMG manually" support tickets.

item.title: v1.0.12
item.description:
• The DM (direct message) feature has been completely removed. X's API and UI have made automated DM sending the #1 trigger for account warnings and rate-limit penalties — the cost-to-benefit was upside-down for every buyer. The agent now focuses on what works without DM risk: replies, tweets, threads, likes, follows, unfollows, and welcome-via-likes for new followers.
  • What got deleted: the entire actions/dm.py module, all DM generators (generate_dm_opener, generate_dm_welcome, generate_dm_reply), the DM session in the afternoon scheduler, the DM follow-up flagging during replies, and all DM-related dashboard UI (Daily DMs input, per-tier "DM after engagement" toggles, "DM from hashtag/home" toggles, "Never DM verified accounts" safety toggle, the DMs stat box).
  • Welcome flow for new followers preserved — but silent. When you gain a follower, the agent still likes 3-4 of their posts as a friendly nod. It just doesn't send a "thanks for the follow!" DM (which X increasingly treats as spam regardless of voice quality).
  • Config keys removed: engagement.daily_dms, per-tier dm_after_engagement / dm_delay_min_minutes / dm_delay_max_minutes, discovery.dm_from_hashtags, discovery.dm_from_home_feed, safety.never_dm_verified_accounts. Existing keys in your config.yaml are ignored and harmless — leave them or remove on next edit.
  • The legacy dm_conversations SQLite table is preserved (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS) so any historical data on existing installs is not lost. No code writes to it anymore. Drop it manually if you want a clean DB.

item.title: v1.0.11
item.description:
• Live X-bio context. The agent now scrapes your own profile (bio, pinned tweet, follower count) once per startup (24h cache) and injects it into every LLM prompt. Result: replies and tweets stop drifting away from your CURRENT positioning — the model knows what your bio says you do, and won't invent contradictory credentials. Cached at data/self_bio.json.
  • Proactive promo discovery. New reply source promo_discovery (default 10% of session budget). Instead of waiting for product keywords to surface randomly in the home feed, the agent actively searches X for tweets matching each promotion's trigger_keywords with a min_faves filter — so product mentions land on visible, relevant conversations. Still capped by promotions.product_reply_max_per_day. Set discovery.promo_discovery_session_share: 0.0 to disable.
  • Auto-suggest watchlist. Once per day (after 9am, only when watchlist has <10 entries), the agent calls the same LLM-driven suggester as the dashboard's ✨ Suggest button and adds up to 2 new accounts at a long 4hr interval. Voice profile required. Conservative caps + long interval mean even occasional LLM hallucinations cause minimal noise — review/edit suggestions in the Discovery → Watchlist panel.
  • Auto-suggested accounts are logged on add so you can spot them in the dashboard log; they default to a 240-min check interval (vs. user-added 60-min) so they earn their place before consuming budget.

item.title: v1.0.10
item.description:
• You can now explicitly allocate session reply budget across discovery sources. 6 new config knobs in discovery: target_session_share, hashtag_session_share, home_session_share, explore_session_share, inspiration_session_share, high_engagement_session_share. Each is a float 0.0-1.0 — set to 0 to disable a source entirely. Example: 50% hashtags + 30% home + 10% targets + 10% explore + 0% inspiration + 0% high-engagement.
  • The bandit still picks ORDER between active sources but no longer overrides allocation — your per-source shares are honored as hard budget caps.
  • Backwards compatible: if a share isn't configured, falls back to legacy behavior (40% inspiration, ~10% explore, ~10% high-engagement, hashtag/home capped by max_*_replies_per_session).

item.title: v1.0.9
item.description:
• CRITICAL: Fixes "Session error — retrying soon" forever loop with 0 actions across the board. v1.0.0 through v1.0.8 all shipped with a packaging bug — the bundled .app was missing the entire actions/ package (reply.py, follow.py, like.py, dm.py, tweet.py, notifications.py). Every session attempt threw ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'actions.reply', the agent caught it as a session error, slept 60s, and retried — endlessly. Symptom: dashboard stats stuck at 0 tweets / 0 replies / 0 follows / 0 likes / 0 DMs across the entire day. Fix: PyInstaller spec now uses collect_submodules for actions/, ai/, agent/, and dashboard/ packages so every module the agent lazily imports is bundled. v1.0.9 actually works.
  • If you were on v1.0.0–v1.0.8 with all-zero stats: install v1.0.9 — the agent will finally start engaging. Manual recovery from a failed install: open Finder → Applications → double-click X-Autopilot.app.

item.title: v1.0.8
item.description:
• Critical fix: auto-update no longer leaves the app dead. v1.0.0 through v1.0.7 had a bug where clicking Install Now would quit the app but never relaunch it (Launch Services bundle cache wasn't refreshed after the swap, and `open -a path` had ambiguous behavior). Symptom: app quits, dashboard tab dies, dock icon disappears. v1.0.8 uses a detached helper script that waits for the parent to die, refreshes the LS cache via lsregister, and launches by path with no -a flag. If you got hit by this on a previous version: open Finder → Applications → double-click X-Autopilot.app to recover. The new bundle is on disk; the OS just didn't relaunch it. After this manual fix, v1.0.8's installer will work for all future updates.
  • One-click "Generate from voice profile" in Settings, above Content Topics. Single LLM call returns niche-appropriate defaults for all 6 content fields (never-say phrases, content topics, voice pillars, signature angles, proof bank, weekly direction). Modal preview with per-field tick + APPEND/OVERWRITE choice. Cost: ~$0.005 on your configured LLM.
  • Auto-post toggle on the Approval Queue page itself — same toggle that was buried in Settings → Posting, now prominent at the top of the queue.
  • Thread auto-approve fixed. Single tweets honored require_approval=false from v1.0.4 but threads always went to manual approval. Now threads auto-approve all parts when auto-post is on.
  • Voice Lab editor copy: "Changes take effect immediately, no agent restart needed."

item.title: v1.0.7
item.description:
• Gemini is now clearly marked as the free option. The provider selector in Settings → API Keys now shows "FREE — no card needed, ~250 replies/day on free tier" next to Gemini, with a green RECOMMENDED badge. Anthropic and OpenAI hints clarify the trial-credit reality so first-time buyers don't accidentally burn $5 in a day.
  • "⚠ HIGH FAIL" badge is now clickable. Hover shows the tooltip ("follow: 47% fail rate (12 samples) — common cause: stale targets that no longer exist"). Click → confirmation dialog → clears the rolling stats for the elevated endpoint(s). Badge disappears instantly after clear.
  • Cleaner messaging: the badge now reads "⚠ HIGH FAIL: FOLLOW (click to clear)" so the action is discoverable.

item.title: v1.0.6
item.description:
• "✨ Suggest from my niche" buttons in Discovery → Hashtags and Discovery → Watchlist. Click → your configured LLM reads your voice profile + niche → returns 8-15 hashtags or 10-15 X accounts active in your space → tick the ones you want → ADD. No more empty-list paralysis after the v1.0.5 cleanup. Cost: ~$0.001-0.005 per click on your own LLM key.
  • Inspiration page now niche-filtered. The agent's /i/jf/creators/inspiration/top_posts scan was surfacing globally-trending posts (cricket scores, celebrity drama) that had nothing to do with your niche. Now each candidate is scored 0.0-1.0 against your voice profile via a tiny cached LLM call; off-topic tweets are dropped before they reach the reply pipeline. Falls back gracefully to "no filtering" if no voice profile is set.
  • Watchlist suggestions show a one-line "why" for each suggested account so you can decide quickly + a "open profile" link to verify the handle exists before adding (LLMs occasionally hallucinate handles).

item.title: v1.0.4
item.description:
• New "Generate Voice Profile" tool in the Voice Lab tab. Paste 50-100 of your recent tweets → click COPY PROMPT → paste into Claude.ai or ChatGPT → paste the structured profile back → SAVE. Done. Every reply and tweet from that point on is anchored to YOUR actual voice instead of generic patterns.
  • Why this matters: the #1 complaint after v1.0.1 was "replies feel generic / off-niche". The root cause is users don't know how to articulate their own voice. The 3000-character extraction prompt gets the LLM to produce an extremely specific profile (identity, niche, tone, linguistic patterns, hook patterns, reference tweets, do/don't rules) — far better than what most users would write themselves.
  • Doesn't burn your in-app API budget — runs externally on Claude.ai or ChatGPT (your choice). One-time onboarding step.
  • The prompt template lives in agent/voice_template.py (version-controlled with the agent) so future tweaks ship via auto-update.
